activities.title: Oral Language Development: Community Circle Time
activities.content:
Greeting
• Welcome pupils and have them sit in a circle. 
• Follow the normal greeting routine.
• Have the pupil that was just greeted, turn to the pupil on their right and greet 
them. This continues all the way around the circle.
• Before school starts, bring in two items related to the theme to show the pupils. 
Put the items in the center of the circle. If no items are available, draw two 
pictures on the board instead.
• Say: Nu xooxkom leek, o sepeerefu "ƥaaɓaan." Tikoorik ke a ndeeree a yoona yo fu 
o sepee.
• Hold up one of the items from the center of the circle. 
• Say: Keek haroo?
• Call on a pupil at random to answer. Say: Har waagaxamo o lay nu keek?
• Call on 2-3 pupils at random to answer. Repeat with the second item. 
• Say: Har tikoorik keek a ndefu yo na in?
• Give pupils one minute to think. You may suggest they close their eyes to picture 
their response. Then choose one of the following options for discussion: call on 
3 pupils at random, Turn and Talk (have pupils turn to a pupil next to them), go 
around the circle and allow every pupil to answer (only if the answer is short), or 
have pupils take turns acting out answers.
• Encourage pupils to bring in their own items relating to the theme throughout the 
week.
Activity
• Play: SONG OR GAME RELATING TO THE THEME

Ga' aam o riiƭ a ƴetaa took faa, 
Ga' aam ƈoox a ƴufaa daaƭlaa,

Keek ndefu ƥaaɓaan.

activities.title: Learning Sounds
activities.content:
Alphabet I-Spy
• Gather all of the letter cards of the letters that have been learned. Place the letter 
cards in different places around the room where the pupils can see the pictures.
• Give pupils a minute to look around to see where the picture cards have been 
placed.
• Say:  Han i mbiyoo o ŋaso ngaa no'ee na "a bootnax". Han no' o hiiƈ, o ga' a ngaa 
nataal o hiiƈ o laa ga, o fool joox nataal ne. I njeeminoo. Ga' aam o ñuxur o jegu /a /. 
• Give pupils a chance to find the picture.
• Say:  O hiiƈee "a" ropu o ñuxuree "arka". I layandoorin: "a", "arka".
• Repeat two times slowly while pointing to the keyword.
• Continue with a few keywords. Be sure to go over letters that have been learned 
thus far.

activities.title: Writing
activities.content:
Learning Names
• Say: Kaa i njagiidaa yo ne i mbindit kaa yo a kon in. Balaa i ndopaa, Han i letin xa 
ƥay in.
• Warm up exercise: have pupils push their palms together as hard as they can for 
10 seconds. Then release and shake hands for 10 seconds. Repeat two more times.
• Give each pupil their individual name card.
• Have pupils go through the following steps: 
1. Pupils trace the letters on the name card with their fingers.
2. Pupils trace the letters of their name on their desks or on the ground. 
3. Pupils write their name on paper. 
• Monitor pupils through each step to make sure they are forming the letters   
 correctly. Provide guidance as needed either verbally or by writing the    
 letter(s) for the pupil to trace.

lessons.homework:
• Ask learners to teach their family members the letter name and sound they learnt  
 today.

Teach and Discuss New Words
• Words: 
siwo  foofi
• Say: I naanga njangaa yo xa ñuxur xa qas pur i mbaag o and a naxee a paax. A 
jega xa ñuxur xa peeñu o ndik na naxee waa i mbarna yo o njang.
• Say the first vocabulary word, but do NOT write it on the board. Then have pupils 
say the word aloud. Repeat two more times.
• Ask pupils what they know about the word. Share the meaning of the word, using 
gestures or illustrations to support understanding. 
• If needed, help pupils understand the word by saying it in another language.
• Repeat all steps with remaining word.

activities.title: Before Reading & Reason to Read
activities.content:
Comprehension: Visualization 
• Say: I ngelaatoo har refu na naxee.
• Read the title of the story but do NOT show the illustration.
• Say:  Na yiif nuun, ndeseñ yo nataal ne nu mboog na yo yee o ten refu na naxee. 
Har nu nga'u? 
• Give the pupils a minute to make the picture in their mind.
• Turn and Talk: Have pupils turn to the pupil next to them to talk about what they 
are visualizing in their minds. After two minutes, gather pupils back as a group. 
Choose a good example you heard from a pupil, and share it with the class.
• Say: Ndiiki, i ƭeetoo nataal ke na naxee koy i ƭeet nam a nandu yo. 
• Show the picture for the story.

• Say:  Har nu nga'u yo nu nataal ne kaa matna o nand fu ke ref'iina na yiif nuun?
• Give the pupils a minute to think about what was the same. Then call on a pupil at 
random asking for what they see. Make sure the pupil's description relates to the 
picture and the story.
Learn New Print Concepts
• Say: Mbanuu i niiraa yo, I naanga yo o niiraa xa ñuxur ake o leng o leng. A nax a 
jega xa ñuxurxa mayu kaa i niiraa yo o leng o leng na lafee. 
• Hold up the book. Read the title slowly and point to each word.
• Call on a pupil at random to come and point to each word of the title as you read.

activities.title: Comprehension: During Reading
activities.content:
Read Aloud (TRANSLATE)  (NEEDS AN ILLUSTRATION)
• Read aloud the story. Point to each word as you read.
A Poxolaacee fa Siwo Foofi le
Meen a red'u reeɗ, a poxolaac a teɓ a ƴiiƴu red'u meen. Kom leng sumu, A 
poxolaacee kaate hoɗom'el a paax. O donumee a weer a weer, too kaate bug'u yer 
foofi. A poxolaacee a layee, "Kaan cuŋkaa a teƥee." Ndaa kom ke a ƥeeraa yo rek, 
too roogfee deɓee. Seƴne a moƴo sumaa rek, koy ngeñ ne a wuuɗaa, ndaa roogfee a 
maad o weer. A poxolaacee a ret a waaƭik foofi. Te ñaaƴ kam xa qol ake koy a ŋaay 
a laxtoox doŋa maak le. Te wootnoox ɗaaŋ a taaƭ ake a waaƭaa o xuluɓ, ndaa ga'ee 
foofi.
Koy, a poxolaacee a ga' kaa jaaxlanduuna, ɗaaŋ ndaxar. Te ref'u a siwo foofi kam a 
pano a qiid. Te ƴuf bo maaga koy a layee, "Nam in waag kaa o yerit na siwo leek?"
A poxolaacee a jeem a ɓuus foofi le fa paayip, ndaa o donumee kaate neew lool. 
Waagee o daaw foofi le. Rek te ga' ɓil a jeem a room a pano le pur te rungin, ndaa xa 
ƴooxum ake kaa de tayil'u yo. Bo ndiik jegee foofi.A poxolaacee ñootee de. Te ƥaat o 
ɗeet o saaxoo saax rek a ga' xa bul xa teɓ. Te jeg pexe. Te samin xa bul ke kam a siwo 
le. O ndaŋ o ndaŋ, te daaw foofi le.
Palak ke, foofi le a daaw o donee na siwo le. A poxolaacee a tuutumaanoox a yer a yer 
bo a heƴ. A poxolaacee a sawar nu xooxum yaam ke te ɗax na soxla um. Rek te a ret, 
a sawar too a heƴ, too a pare an ke te fi' ka taa.

activities.title: Comprehension: After Reading
activities.content:
Factual Question: Review All
• Read the title of the story. Call on a pupil at random to answer each of the 
following factual questions:
 Question 1: Har a poxolaacee a waaɗee gu? ( foofi) 
 Question 2: Tam a poxolaacee a ga' tu foofi le? (kam a siwo)
• After each response, ask the pupil why they gave that answer. Affirm the correct 
answer or attempt, let them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer. Help 
pupils find the part of the story that contains the answer.

Inferential Questions: Main Idea
• Say: A nax nuu refna a jega o sepaa te lalit na. O ten refu ke refna na nax ale. Ke 
a nax ale lalit na refu a poxolaacee ahe waaɗaa foofi. Keek a taxa bo in foogee ke 
moƴna o may na naxee refu a poxolaacaa naa waaɗaa naa te jegit kaa foofi.
• Ask the pupils if they agree.
• Say:  Ke jegna kam a nax ale "A poxolaacee fa a siwo le", refu ne, a poxolaacee 
jegit na foofi yaam, ke moƴna may na naxee refu ahe waaɗaa foofi.
• Repeat the sentence but prompt pupils to finish the sentence by saying what the   
 story is mostly about.

•  Ask learners to teach their family members the new vocabulary words they learnt  
 today.

activities.title: Learning Sounds
activities.content:
Sound Matching Game
• Write the letters that have been learned on the board. 
• The letters should be large enough for all pupils to see. Make sure they are evenly 
spaced out in a line that is eye level for the pupils. After writing each letter:
• Say: Har refu o hiiƈeek? Har refu o nanelum?
• Call on a pupil at random to answer. Affirm the correct answer or attempt, let 
them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer.
• Put the pupils into pairs and give each pair a letter card (use only the letters that 
have been learned so far). Have the pairs sit in a line facing the board.
• Say:  In fiya ngaa o nanel too te ref o hiiƈee refna na karta le damoona, nuun fo 
xaariitof nu atiid a karta le jegna o hiiƈee koy ndendadin fo o hiiƈee na tabla le. 
• When pupils go to the board with their letter card, affirm the correct answer or 
attempt, let them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer.
• Go through the letters that have been learned. Assist pupils as needed if they are 
having difficulty connecting the sound said with their letter card.
• As time permits, switch up the letter cards between the pairs of pupils.

• Say: Han i ŋas o ŋas. Han lalanuun gon leng ohuu te refna gonum rek, o gar nu 
njasnoor koy lay gonof lay kalaas ne de mbi' mañeer ƭik. 
• Hold up a name card. If the pupil is unable to recognize the name, say it aloud.
• Once the child comes up front, have them give two actions for the class. For 
example, "[Name] says touch your toes. [Name] says jump twice."
• Continue with several pupils as time permits.

picture and the story.

following factual questions:
Question 1: Har Kariim a bug'u? (ɓanaana fumangaru) 
Question 2:  Tam xa soraas ake ndef u? (Na mbaawee)
• After each response, ask the pupil why they gave that answer. Affirm the correct 
answer or attempt, let them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer. Help 
pupils find the part of the story that contains the answer. 

Inferential Questions: Main Idea
• Say:  A nax nuu refna, a jega o no'tand. O no'tandee refu ke a naxee a layaa. Ke 
moƴna may na xa laf ake na naxeek, ga'aam o ƥiy o ngoor fa a koy de mbaaƭaa yo

a ndamrit'iina pur de mbaaƭ xa ƥiy taxar kaa de ñaam na yo, yaam ke moƴna o may

• Welcome pupils and have them sit in a circle. 
• Follow the normal greeting routine.
• Have the pupil that was just greeted, turn to the pupil on their right and greet 
them. This continues all the way around the circle.
• Before school starts, bring in two items related to the theme to show the pupils. 
Put the items in the center of the circle. If no items are available, draw two 
pictures on the board instead.
• Say: Nu xooxkom leek, o sepee refu "O nged." Tikoorik ke naa layaa in ke ref na 
no sepee.
•  Hold up one of the items from the center of the circle.
• Say: Keek haroo?
• Call on a pupil at random to answer. 
• Say: Har waagaxamo lay nu keek?
• Call on 2-3 pupils at random to answer. Repeat with the second item. 
• Say: An naa topatooxaa o nged nuun ?
• Give pupils one minute to think, even close their eyes to picture their response. 
Then choose one of the following options for discussion: call on pupils at random, 
Turn and Talk (have pupils turn to a pupil next to them), go around the circle and 
allow every pupil to answer (only if the answer is short), or have pupils take turns 
acting out answers.

week.

activities.content:
Sound Matching Game
• Write the letters that have been learned on the board. (a, b, c) The letters should 
be large enough for all pupils to see. Make sure they are evenly spaced out in a 
line that is eye level for the pupils. After writing each letter:
• Say: Har refu o hiiƈeek? Nanel o lum o hiiƈu leek a jegu??
• Call on a pupil at random to answer. Affirm the correct answer or attempt, let 
them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer.
• Put the pupils into pairs and give each pair a letter card (use only the letters that 
have been learned so far). Have the pairs sit in a line facing the board.
• Say:  Han fi' o nanel koy o jega ngaa a karta le jegna o hiiƈee, nuun fa xaariitof nu 
mbool bo na tabla le koy nu taƥin a karta le no hiiƈee. 
• When pupils go to the board with their letter card, affirm the correct answer or 
attempt, let them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer.
• Go through the letters that have been learned. Assist pupils as needed if they are 
having difficulty connecting the sound said with their letter card.
• As time permits, switch up the letter cards between the pairs of pupils.

activities.title: Alphabet
activities.content:
Name Card
• Gather all the pupil name cards. 
• Say: Han i ŋas o ŋas. I janga ngaa a karta laa jegna a kon koy o ga' maaga gonof, o 
gar nu njasnoor koy o lay gonof. Ndiiki, nu njil ka yii o ŋas o leng koy nu mbiyin fu 
qaariit nuun. 
• Hold up a name card. If the pupil is unable to recognize the name, say it aloud.
• Once the child comes up front, have them give two actions for the class. For 
example, "[Name] says touch your toes. [Name] says jump twice."
• Continue with several pupils as time permits.

• Say: Keek refu o hiiƈee nu xoox kom le. O hiiƈeek o ten refu o nanel /d/. I

sure they have the right letter. Ask pupils what letter they are writing.

jega o piibind. 
• Point to the author's name on the storybook.
• Say:  O piibind ohe refu ohe bind na a naxee. An refu o piibind safe? 
• Give pupils a moment to think, then call on a pupil at random to answer. Affirm the 
correct answer or attempt, let them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer by 
repeating, "the author is the person who wrote the story."

• Point to the illustrator's name on the storybook.
• Say: O teedeseñ refu ohe naa deseñaa nataal pogreer. An refu o teedeseñ nataal? 
• Give pupils a moment to think, then call on a pupil at random to answer. Affirm the 
correct answer or attempt, let them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer by 
repeating, "the illustrator is the person who drew the pictures."
• Say: A nax nuu refna a jega o no'tand. 
• Point to the title on the storybook.
• Say:  O no'tand o ten refu o no'tandee na naxee. Har refu o no'tand a nax?
• Give pupils a moment to think, then call on a pupil at random to answer. Affirm the 
correct answer or attempt, let them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer by

activities.title: Vocabulary

meeñ  marse

say the word aloud. Repeat two more times.
• Ask pupils what they know about the word. Share the meaning of the word, using 
gestures or illustrations to support understanding.
• If needed, help pupils understand the word by saying it in another language.

activities.title: Before Reading & Reason to Read
activities.content:
Comprehension: Visualization 
• Say:  Ndigiloo i niir a yo a naxeek, fat i mbi' na yiif in nataal ne i mboogna yo yee o 
ten refu na naxee.
• Read the title of the story but do NOT show the illustration.
• Say:  Nu yiifof, deseñi ke foogoona yee o ten refu na nax ale. Har ga' o? 
• Give the pupils a minute to make the picture in their mind.
• Turn and Talk: Have pupils turn to the pupil next to them to talk about what they 
are visualizing in their minds. After two minutes, gather pupils back as a group. 
Choose a good example you heard from a pupil, and share it with the class.
• Say: Ndiiki, i ƭeetoo nataal ke na naxee koy i ƭeet nam a nandu yo. 
• Show the picture for the story.
• Say: Har nu nga'u yo nu nataal ne kaa matna o nand fu ke ref'iina na yiif nuun.

• Give the pupils a minute to think about what was the same. Then call on a pupil at 
random asking for what they see. Make sure the pupil's description relates to the 
picture and the story.
Learn New Print Concepts
• Say: Mbanuu i niiraa yo, i naanga yo o niiraa xa ñuxur ake o leng o leng. A nax a 
jega xa ñuxur xa mayu kaa i niiraa yo o leng o leng na lafee.
• Hold up the book. Read the title slowly and point to each word.
• Call on a pupil at random to come and point to each word of the title as you read.

activities.title: Comprehension: During Reading
activities.content:
Read Aloud
• Read aloud the story. Point to each word as you read.
Elisabet Fa xa Ƥeem xa Tew xa Ƭaq
Kom leng, Elisabet fu xa ƥiyum xa tew xa ƭaq awe moof'a yo o mbiñ o leng. A we no'e 
yo Maryaama fa Lusi. Samdi fa leng, Elisabet a lay xa ƥeem xa tew ake yee, "I ndetoo 
na marse faa." Te layee, Maryaama, wo' naa roxondoox kaa xa mangaru ke, Lusi wo' 
naa roxondoox kaa pom fee. Mi'
han roxondoo anaanaas fee, Maryaama a layee, "iyo, han roxondoox a den." Ndaa 
Lusi a layee, "Ha'aa, Roxondoox kiim a den." Ndiiki Elisabet a woxoox o xeqee koy a 
roxondoor anaanaas fee. Maryaama a roxondoox xa mangaru ke fu pom fee. Ndaa 
Lusi o ten roxondooxee dara.
Na samdi fa lakas faa, Elisabet a layee, "Maryaama, haye wo naa roxondoox kaa 
pom fee. Lusi wo naa roxondoox kaa xa mangaru ke. Han roxondoox anaanaas fee 
koy woxoox o xeqee. Maryaama a layeee, "Iyo han roxondoox a den." Koy Lusi layee, 
"Ha'aa mi roxondoox kiim a den." Ndiiki Elisabet a woxoox o xeqee koy a roxondoox 
anaanaas fee. Maryaama a roxondoox xa mangaru ke fu pom fee fop. Ndaa ahin, Lusi 
o ten roxondooxee dara.
Samdi fa leng, Maryaama a layee, "mi' kaan jir" Elisabet a layee, "I ndetoo nu 
lopitaan naa." Ndaa Maryaama a layee, "I ndetoo na marse faa. I inooxa ngaa 
maaga, han i ndetoo nu lopitaan naa." Ndiiki Elisabet a woxoox o xeqee koy a 
roxondoox anaanaas fee. Maryaama a roxondoox
xa mangaru ke fu pom fee fop. Ndaa Lusi o ten roxondooxee dara. Ndiiki Maryaama 
kaa te jir'u lool too a xer. Te meeñ koy Lusi a gis xa mangaru ke fu pom fee. Te dam o 
ɓayee no maagum koy a dimble in te inoox. Te woxoox a Maryaama koy a layee, "Yaa, 
i ƥisoo a Maryaama lopitaan ndiiki ndiiki. Hotit na haye, mi' naa bug kaa o ɓisaa a ƥiy

activities.title: Comprehension: After Reading
activities.content:
Factual Question: Review All
• Read the title of the story. Call on a pupil at random to answer each of the 
following factual questions:
Question 1:Tam a ƥiseegu yo xa ƥiy taxar ake? (na marse faa) 
Question 2:Har daaw'u a Maryaama? (kaa te a jir'u/ a meeñ)

• After each response, ask the pupil why they gave that answer. Affirm the correct 
answer or attempt, let them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer. Help 
pupils find the part of the story that contains the answer.
Inferential Questions: Main Idea
• Say: A nax nuu refna, a jega o no'tand. O no'tandee refu ke a naxee a layaa. Na 
naxee nanaam ne a kangaam ake a ndoxondooxit iina yo tikoorik den ke a ndet na 
marse faa. Na naxee tamin a lalita a Lusi jaɓee o damit o leng. Keek a taxa bo in 
foogee ke moƴa may na naxee ahe lalitaa ne i mbar na yo o ndamirit. 
• Ask the pupils if they agree.
• Say:  No no'tandee na naxee "Elisabet Fa Xa Ƥeem Xa Tew Xa Ƭaq" a lalta o njeriñ 
ndamir yaam, ke moƴna o may na naxee ahe laltaa o tew o haa fañ na o dimble 
fogum we/ ƥasilum.
• Repeat the sentence but prompt pupils to finish the sentence by saying what the   
 story is mostly about.

lessons.homework:
• Ask learners to teach their family members the new vocabulary words they learnt  
 today.

activities.content:
Greeting
• Welcome pupils and have them sit in a circle. 
• Follow the normal greeting routine.
• Have the pupil that was just greeted, turn to the pupil on their right and greet 
them. This continues all the way around the circle.

pictures on the board instead.
• Say:  Nu xooxkom le o sepee refu "A qaaj ke nu njer." Tikoorik ke ndefna a 
ndeeree a yoona fu o sepee.
• Hold up one of the items from the center of the circle. 
• Say: Keek haroo?
• Call on a pupil at random to answer. 
• Say: Har waagaxamo o lay nu keek?
• Call on 2-3 pupils at random to answer. Repeat with the second item.
• Say: A qaajum moƴoŋ o fel no ɓaalof?
• Give pupils one minute to think, even close their eyes to picture their response. 
Then choose one of the following options for discussion: call on pupils at random, 
Turn and Talk (have pupils turn to a pupil next to them), go around the circle and 
allow every pupil to answer (only if the answer is short), or have pupils take turns 
acting out answers.

week.

activities.title: Learning Sounds
activities.content:
Sound Matching Game
• Write the letters that have been learned on the board. The letters should be large 
enough for all pupils to see. Make sure they are evenly spaced out in a line that is 
eye level for the pupils. After writing each letter:
• Say: Har refu o hiiƈeek? Har refu o nanel o hiiƈeek?
• Call on a pupil at random to answer. Affirm the correct answer or attempt, let 
them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer.
• Put the pupils into pairs and give each pair a letter card (use only the letters that 
have been learned so far). Have the pairs sit in a line facing the board.
• Say: Han fi' o nanel koy a refangaa na karta le saqoona, nuun fa xaariitof nu mbool 
ndet na tabla le taƥin a karta le no hiiƈee.
• When pupils go to the board with their letter card, affirm the correct answer or 
attempt, let them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer.
• Go through the letters that have been learned. Assist pupils as needed if they are 
having difficulty connecting the sound said with their letter card.
• As time permits, switch up the letter cards between the pairs of pupils.

activities.title: Alphabet
activities.content:
Name Card #4
• Gather all the pupil name cards. 
• Say: Han i ŋasoo o ŋas. In yoɗa ngaa a karta laa jegna gon too o ga' gonof teen, 
o gar nu njasnoor lay gonof. Ndiiki njang yo o ŋas o leng koy nuun fu xaariitof nu 
mbiyin.
• Hold up a name card. If the pupil is unable to recognize the name, say it aloud.
• Once the child comes up front, have them give two actions for the class. For 
example, "[Name] says touch your toes. [Name] says jump twice."
• Continue with several pupils as time permits.

activities.title: Letter of the Week
activities.content:
Learning Letter: "f F"
• Write the small letter "f" very big on the board. Point to the letter.
• Say:  Keek refu o hiiƈee nu xooxkom le. O nanelee nu hiiƈeek refu /f/. I layandoor 
/f/. 

• Hold up the letter card.
• Say: /f/ O ten refu o hiiƈeek ropna o ñuxur "famb". /f/ ropu o ñuxuree "famb". 
• Have pupils repeat: "f", "famb"

activities.title: Writing
activities.content:
Learning Names
• Say:  Kaa i njangii daa ne i mbinit kaa a kon in. Balaa i ndopaa, han i letin xa ƥay in.
• Warm up exercise: have pupils push their palms together as hard as they can for 
10 seconds. Then release and shake hands for 10 seconds. Repeat two more times.
• Give each pupil their individual name card. 
• Have pupils go through the following steps: 
1. Pupils trace the letters on the name card with their fingers.
2. Pupils trace the letters of their name on their desks or on the ground.
3. Pupils write their name on paper. 
• Monitor pupils through each step to make sure they are forming the letters 
correctly. Provide guidance as needed either verbally or by writing the letter(s) for 
the pupil to trace.

• Say: Ga'aam tigaa jegna o nanel kom /f/. Kaaga haroo?

• Gather pupils outside in a circle. Take the letter cards with you.
• Say: Han i njang ne i mbinit kaa xa qiiƈ xa pogreer. Han lay gon le nu hiiƈee koy nu 
njang qol nuun nu mbindin a lang.
• Say one of the letters that have been learned.

sure they have the right letter. Ask pupils what letter they are writing.

board.

activities.title: Reason to Read
activities.content:
Learn New Print Concepts
• Find a children's storybook with an author and illustrator.
• Think about how books and stories have different parts.

• Say: Mbanuu i niiraa, han i nga' tigaa nguutatir na kam a naxee. A nax nuu refna a 
jega o piibind.
• Point to the author's name on the storybook.
• Say:  O piibind ohe refu ohe bind na a naxee. An refu o piibind safe? 
• Give pupils a moment to think, then call on a pupil at random to answer. Affirm the 
correct answer or attempt, let them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer by 
repeating, "the author is the person who wrote the story."
• Say: A nax nuu ga'oona a jega o teedeseñ.
• Point to the illustrator's name on the storybook.
• Say: O teedeseñ refu ohe naa deseñaa nataal pogreer. An refu o teedeseñ nataal?
• Give pupils a moment to think, then call on a pupil at random to answer. Affirm the 
correct answer or attempt, let them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer by 
repeating, "the illustrator is the person who drew the pictures."
• Say: A nax nuu refna a jega o no'tand.
•  Point to the title on the storybook.
• Say:  O no'tand o ten refu o no'tandee na naxee. Har refu o no'tand a nax?
• Give pupils a moment to think, then call on a pupil at random to answer. Affirm the 
correct answer or attempt, let them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer by 
repeating, "the title is what the story is called."
• Say: I naangaa niiraa, i niira yii xa ñuxur ake o leng o leng. A nax a naanga jegaa 
xa ñuxur xa kaa i niira o leng o leng na laf nuu refna. 
• Write the following sentence on the board: Maryaama a yena yii koy te meeñ. 
• Call on a pupil at random to come and point to each word of the setence as you 
read aloud.

activities.content:

• Read the title of the first story, pointing to each word, and show the illustration. 
• Say:  Han lay a nuun tigaa xewna na naxee. Nu njangoo nataal ne fu kenu lay iina 
na naxee koy nu njeem pur cooɗit o ngelaat nu ke in layaa.
• Choose a character, animal, or object from the story that is also in the illustration. 
Give three clues for pupils to try and guess.
• Call on a pupil at random to answer. Affirm the correct answer or attempt, let 
them know if it is correct, and call on another pupil if incorrect.
• Repeat two more times. A different illustration from the story can be chosen if   
 needed.

•  Ask learners to tell their family members what they learnt about who a writer and  
 an  illustrator of a book are.

activities.content:

• Gather the letter cards for the letters that have been learned:  A-B-C-D-E-F
• Say: Han i ƥaat o njang a cang in na xa qiɓ. Mbetandoox yo yee, xa qiɓ no ñuxur a 
fogu. 
• Hold up one of the letter cards showing the keyword. Say the keyword slowly, 
clapping each syllable.

• Say:  I mboxandoor xa ƥay in koy layoo o ñuxuree took.
• Clap the syllables for the keyword, monitoring students as they follow along. 
• Say: Ndiiki koy nuuno yoo pur o njeem. Han lal a nuun o ñuxur koy nu mboxan xa 
qiɓ ake no ñuxur o feeñu le. 
• Put the pupils into pairs and give each a letter card. Go around to each pair and 
have them clap the syllables for the keyword.
• NOTE: Monitor which students are able to separate syllables correctly. If a pupil 
is having difficulty, stand next to them and help them try clapping the syllables. 
Extension: give each pair of pupils a different letter card to clap the syllables.

activities.title: Letter of the Week
activities.content:
Assessing Sounds Learned in Term 2
• Gather the letter cards for the letters learned this term: (a -b- c -d- e -f ) 
INSERT THE LETTERS LEARNT
• Put the letter cards in different places around the room (example: on the floor, on 
the wall). Give pupils a minute to walk around the room and look to see where each 
letter is found.
• Create five teams of pupils. Call a team and say a letter sound. When the pupils 
in that team hear the sound, they are to run to the letter card that makes that 
sound. After the team runs to a letter, say the sound again. Ask the other teams if 
the think the first team is correct. Affirm the correct answer or clarify if it is not 
the correct answer. Continue with each group having a turn to find the matching 
letter.
• NOTE: Keep track of which pupils or teams are having difficulty recognizing 
specific letters. Also see if there is a specific letter most of the class is struggling 
with. If this happens, stop and review the letter before continuing with the game.

activities.title: Comprehension: Before Reading
activities.content:
Making Connections
• Say: Nu xooxkom leek o sepee refu "Pind fu Kenand".Han i niir a naxee no "Pind 
kuutatiru pur wiin nguutatiru."
• Call on a pupil at random to answer. Affirm the correct answer or attempt, let 
them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer.
• Say: Balaa i mburle aa niiraa yo ke yoqna na naxee, i layoo ke i mbogna yo fa 
naxee. Har tikoorik ke na naxee a njegu yo fa nuun? 
• Give pupils one minute to think and then call on a pupil at random to answer. If 
pupils are having difficulty, give an example and ask if that it is true for them too. 
Example: Once I saw butterflies on a plant. 
• NOTE: Be sure to ask different pupils throughout the week. If a pupil is struggling, 
ask them prompting questions, such as: Have you ever [insert event from story]? 
Monitor and keep track of how well the pupils are able to make connections that 
make sense and relate to the story.

activities.title: Comprehension: During Reading
activities.content:
Read Aloud
• Read aloud the story. 
A ndok kee na Faatu a maxte yii nen o ɗaakaan. Maryaama a laamitin, a layinee, 
"Kum taxu a ndok fee a jigid lool?"
Faatu a layinee, "O maag ole a mayin a ngaa kam ndiig, foofi le a naanga yii o 
rokiidaa. O ɗaakaandee naa taxaa bo kam tok in ke nguɓ kee!"
Maryaama a ɗeetik a xaariitum Laamin. Ƥasilum gaynaak a ndefu yo too a yoonaa 
yo fu naak den. Laamin ngenandum xa loq fu xa sar a jagand te. Laamin a layee, "I 
naangaa mbirlooxaa mbaadaa daaƭ pur muumiim/ƥaaɓaan in ke. I yoona yii fu pind in 
ke.
Maryaama xelaat pind ke fop. Koy a layee, "Mbind nuu refna a guutatira fu gendum, 
ndaa mbind nuu refna a naanga hiiraa wiin we koy de ndef na jam."
    
Pind fop a mbaaxa a ref a ngaa yee a naanga ngiiraa ƥasil ke. 

• Stop at the end of the first part of the story.
• Say:  Har foogo yee o ten naa xew ka taa? Mbuul yo a kid nuun koy ngelaat ke nu 
mboog na yee o ten naa xew kaa.
• Call on a pupil at random to give their prediction. After the answer, ask why they 
made the prediction. Call on another pupil to give their answer. 
• NOTE: Be sure to ask different pupils throughout the week. If a pupil is struggling, 
ask them prompting questions, such as: What happened in the story? What could 
the character do next? Monitor and keep track of how well the pupils are able to 
make predictions that make sense and relate to the story.

activities.title: Comprehension: After Reading
activities.content:
Factual & Inferential Question: Review All
• Before the lesson, gather cards with the following question words (one word per 
card): Who? What? Where? When? Why?
• Call on a pupil at random to come take a card from you. Read the corresponding 
factual question aloud and have the pupil answer.
WHO: An ret'u a ɗeetik a Maryaama? (Laamin)
WHAT: Har Faatu a layu a Maryaama na ndokumee? (Jangi xa toonooƭ ake layee 
na yo nu ne a ndokee a haar teel)
WHERE: Tam a ndokee na Faatu a maxe? (paam o maag ole)  
WHEN: Mban o maag ole maayinaa? (kam ndiig,)
WHY:  Kum taxu pind ke nguutatir?  (jangi xa toonooɗ nuu jaajand we a lay na yo)
• After each response, ask the pupil why they gave that answer. Affirm the correct 
answer or attempt, let them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer. Continue 
through all questions. 
• NOTE: Be sure to ask different pupils each day to answer questions. If a pupil is 
not able to answer, reread the part of the story that has the answer. See if the 
pupil can respond correctly. If not, explain the correct response. Monitor and keep 
track of pupils having difficulty, and consider how to give them extra support.

• NOTE: Be sure to ask different pupils throughout the week. Remember to ask   
 prompting questions if a pupil is struggling.

activities.title: Learning Sounds
activities.content:
Sound Matching Game
• Write the following letters on the board: LETTER LEARNED IN THE TERM    (a-bc-d-e-f)
• The letters should be large enough for all pupils to see. Make sure they are evenly 
spaced out in a line that is eye level for the pupils. After writing each letter:
• Say: Har refu o hiiƈeek? Har refu o nanelum? 
• Call on a pupil at random to answer. Affirm the correct answer or attempt, let 

them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer.
• Put the pupils into pairs and give each pair a letter card (use only the letters that 
have been learned so far). Have the pairs sit in a line facing the board.
• Say:  Han fi' o nanel koy a ref a ngaa o hiiƈee na karta le saqoona, nuun fa xaariitof 
nu mbool ndet na tabla le taƥin a karta le no hiiƈee. 
• When pupils go to the board with their letter card, affirm the correct answer or 
attempt, let them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer.
• Go through the letters that have been learned. Assist pupils as needed if they are 
having difficulty connecting the sound said with their letter card.
• As time permits, switch up the letter cards between the pairs of pupils.
• NOTE: Keep track of which pupils are having difficulty recognizing specific letters. 
Also see if there is a specific letter most of the class is struggling with. If this 
happens, stop and review the letter before continuing with the game.

activities.title: Writing
activities.content:
Reviewing Names
• Say:  Kaa i ƥaat kaa yo o njang ne i mbindit kaa a kon in. Balaa i ndopaa, han i letin 
xa ƥay in.
• Warm up exercise: have pupils tap their fingers one at a time on their thumb (start 
with pointer, then middle, then ring, then pinky). Do one hand at a time. As pupils 
learn the movement, try doing both hands at the same time.
• Give each pupil their individual name card. 
• NOTE: Have pupils write their name on their paper. If pupils cannot complete their 
name, try to find a way to help them. For example, write the letters and have them 
trace. Another option: see if pupils are able to write their name without looking at 
their name card.

activities.title: Alphabet
activities.content:
Name Card
• Put all of the pupils' name cards on the floor or table. 
• Say: Ohuu hooyuuma pur te gar nu njasnoor, o ɗeet gonof. O ga'a ngaa gonof, o 
cooɗaam a karta le. 
• Have pupils come up 2-3 at a time. When they bring you their card, point to their 
name and as they say it move your finger along the letters. Then have the pupil 
clap the syllables in their name.
• NOTE: Monitor which pupils are able to identify their name and clap the syllables, 
and those pupils who have difficulty. If pupils don't recognize their name, try to 
find a way to help them remember it. For example, write it in large print on their 
notebook or a piece of spare paper. Ask them to take it home and trace the letters 
with their finger a few times. If pupils have difficulty clapping the syllables in their 
name, clap with them as you slowly say their name.
